extracted.intended_audience: systematic review authors, meta-analysts, and peer reviewers assessing randomized and non-randomized intervention studies
extracted.subtask_description: Applying Cochrane's recommended tools (RoB 2 for RCTs, ROBINS-I for non-randomised studies) and the GRADE framework to assess risk of bias in individual studies and the certainty/quality of the body of evidence for systematic reviews and clinical guidance. Includes domain-level judgments and reviewer checks for appropriate tool use and justification of ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality vs. Risk of Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cochrane Handbook draws a distinction between assessment of methodological quality and assessment of risk of bias, and recommends a focus on the latter. The key consideration is the extent to which results of included studies should be believed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing studies for inclusion in a review, emphasize risk of bias (threats to internal validity and whether results are believable) rather than broad or ill-defined notions of 'quality'.

rubrics_metrics.name: RoB 2: Bias arising from the randomization process
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias arising from the randomization process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of five RoB 2 domains; recommended for randomized clinical trials. Consider allocation sequence generation, allocation concealment, baseline imbalances that suggest a problem with randomization.

rubrics_metrics.name: RoB 2: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions (effect of assignment / effect of adhering)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of five RoB 2 domains; evaluate whether departures from the assigned intervention occurred and whether those deviations bias the estimate of the effect of assignment or of adherence as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: RoB 2: Bias due to missing outcome data
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias due to missing outcome data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of five RoB 2 domains; assess the amount, reasons, and handling of missing data and whether missingness could bias results.

rubrics_metrics.name: RoB 2: Bias in measurement of the outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias in measurement of the outcome
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of five RoB 2 domains; consider blinding of outcome assessors, validity and reliability of outcome measurement, and differential measurement across groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: RoB 2: Bias in selection of the reported result
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias in selection of the reported result
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of five RoB 2 domains; assess selective reporting (e.g., multiple outcomes/analyses with choice of favorable results), availability of protocols, and consistency between reported analyses and prespecified plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: RoB 2 domain-level judgments (classification categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each RoB 2 domain receives: Low risk of bias; Some concerns; High risk of bias
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these standardized judgments for each domain; use signaling questions in the RoB 2 tool to guide choices. These domain judgments feed into an overall risk-of-bias judgment for the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROBINS-I: Confounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Confounding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of seven ROBINS-I domains for non-randomised studies; assess whether measured or unmeasured confounders could have distorted the intervention effect (consider pre-intervention differences and adjustment strategies).

rubrics_metrics.name: ROBINS-I: Selection of participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of participants
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of seven ROBINS-I domains; evaluate whether the way participants were selected into the study or into the analysis could introduce bias (e.g., selection related to both intervention and outcome).

rubrics_metrics.name: ROBINS-I: Classification of interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of interventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of seven ROBINS-I domains; assess misclassification of intervention status (timing, dose, fidelity) and whether such misclassification is differential or non-differential.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROBINS-I: Deviations from intended interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Deviations from intended interventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of seven ROBINS-I domains; consider post-intervention deviations, co-interventions, adherence, and whether these deviations bias effect estimates in non-randomised contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROBINS-I: Missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of seven ROBINS-I domains; evaluate the extent, reasons, and handling of missing outcome or covariate data and potential bias from loss to follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROBINS-I: Measurement of outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement of outcomes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of seven ROBINS-I domains; assess validity and reliability of outcome measurement and whether measurement differs by intervention status.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROBINS-I: Selection of the reported result
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of the reported result
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of seven ROBINS-I domains; evaluate selective reporting and deviations from analysis plans that could bias reported findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE component: Risk of bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk of bias
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In GRADE, risk of bias at the study level contributes to the certainty assessment of the body of evidence. Downgrade overall confidence if studies are at serious or very serious risk of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE component: Directness (indirectness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Directness (indirectness)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the evidence directly answers the review question (participants, interventions, comparators, outcomes); indirectness can lower confidence in estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE component: Heterogeneity (inconsistency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Heterogeneity (inconsistency)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider variability in results across studies (direction and magnitude); unexplained inconsistency can reduce certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE component: Precision (imprecision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Precision (imprecision)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate confidence intervals and the number of events/participants; wide confidence intervals or sparse data may lead to downgrading for imprecision.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE component: Publication bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication bias
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the likelihood that available studies are a non-representative subset of all studies (e.g., small-study effects, selective publication); suspected publication bias can lower the quality rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE: Quality ratings for the body of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality ratings: High, Moderate, Low, Very Low
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the GRADE approach to rate overall certainty of a body of evidence across studies, starting at 'High' for RCT evidence and downgrading for the GRADE components listed above (or upgrading observational evidence where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer check: Was risk of bias assessed appropriately?
rubrics_metrics.description: When peer reviewing systematic reviews or original clinical trials, reviewers should check whether risk of bias was assessed appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for use of validated tools, clear application of domain criteria, transparency in judgments, and whether assessment methods match the study designs being reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer check: Was the right tool used (RoB 2 or ROBINS-I)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should check whether the right tool (RoB 2 or ROBINS-I) was used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RoB 2 is recommended for randomized clinical trials; ROBINS-I is appropriate for non-randomised intervention studies. Using the wrong tool can mischaracterize bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer check: Are GRADE ratings justified?
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should check whether GRADE ratings are justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that downgrades/upgrades are explicitly linked to the GRADE components (risk of bias, directness, heterogeneity, precision, publication bias) with clear reasoning and supporting data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer check: Is the certainty of evidence appropriately stated?
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should check whether the certainty of evidence is appropriately stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that the review's conclusions reflect the GRADE overall ratings (High/Moderate/Low/Very Low) and that language about confidence/uncertainty is consistent with those ratings.
